facts.fact_text: Immediately after the announcement of the preliminary results of the 19 February 2008 Armenian presidential election, Mr Levon Ter-Petrosyan called on his supporters to gather at Freedom Square in central Yerevan in order to protest against alleged irregularities in the election process.
The rallies at Freedom Square attracted at times tens of thousands of people.
The applicant regularly attended the demonstrations held at Freedom Square in Yerevan.
The applicant gave speeches at the demonstrations held at Freedom Square in Yerevan.
On 1 March 2008, at some point around 6-7 a.m., a police operation was conducted at Freedom Square in Yerevan where several hundred demonstrators were camping.
The applicant alleged that the aim of the police operation on 1 March 2008 at Freedom Square had been forcibly to terminate the assembly.
The applicant alleged that a large police force had violently attacked the demonstrators at Freedom Square with rubber batons and electric shock devices, without any prior warning.
The applicant alleged that the police attack on demonstrators at Freedom Square on 1 March 2008 forced the demonstrators to flee the square.
The Government alleged that the applicant and the group of opposition supporters whom he had joined had conspired to usurp State power.
The Government alleged that the assembly at Freedom Square had pursued the aim of usurping State power by discrediting the presidential election.
The Government alleged that the assembly at Freedom Square had pursued the aim of usurping State power by creating illusions of public discontent and revolt.
The Government alleged that the assembly at Freedom Square had pursued the aim of usurping State power by destabilising the internal political situation.
